subquestion: Q4: choose A/B volume fractions minimizing material cost while conduction probability is at least 0.90
target_claim: Return the lowest-cost independently verified A/B mixture found on a declared two-dimensional search domain whose 95% Wilson lower bound for conduction is at least 0.90, and distinguish best-verified from globally optimal.

leakage_risks: selecting and confirming on the same random streams
pruning mixtures using an unvalidated monotonic assumption
data_audit.missingness_notes: No closed-form mixed percolation law is supplied; A/B interactions must be simulated explicitly.

baseline.name: pure-A and pure-B feasible cost comparison
baseline.reason: Provides interpretable endpoints and a guaranteed comparator for any claimed benefit from mixing.
baseline.implementation: Find confidence-feasible pure-A and pure-B points using the Q3 protocol and evaluate the official cost function.
baseline.validation: Every mixed candidate must have cost no worse than the best independently confirmed pure endpoint to justify added complexity.

candidates.name: confidence-constrained two-dimensional mixture search
candidates.formulation: Simulate explicit A capsules and B spheres with A-A, A-B and B-B exact predicates. Evaluate a coarse (phi_A,phi_B) grid, retain confidence-feasible and near-boundary points, refine locally along the estimated feasibility frontier, and minimize 1000*(1.05 phi_A+0.05 phi_B) CNY. Confirm the final candidate and nearby cheaper points with independent seeds.
assumptions: A and B centers are uniform and mutually independent in the periodic cube.
The stated linear material cost applies to achieved volume fractions.
Adding conductors cannot reduce connectivity under coupled configurations.
validation_plan: audit all three pair predicates against independent distance calculations
check non-dominated frontier and locally cheaper neighbors
confirm final and cheaper-neighbor candidates on held-out seeds
refutation_evidence: mixture does not improve on the best pure endpoint
a tested cheaper neighbor is also confidence-feasible
held-out Wilson lower bound falls below 0.90
pair predicates disagree with exact checks
candidates.decision_reason: It represents mixed geometry explicitly and ties the cost decision to conservative statistical feasibility.

candidates.name: coarse non-dominated grid with independent confirmation
candidates.formulation: Evaluate a fixed preregistered grid over achieved A/B particle counts, discard cost-dominated points, and independently confirm the cheapest point whose Wilson lower bound reaches 0.90 without response-surface interpolation.
assumptions: The declared fixed grid is adequate for a best-verified discrete recommendation.
The same mixed placement mechanism as the primary candidate.
validation_plan: repeat cheapest feasible and immediate cheaper points with independent seeds
refutation_evidence: a cheaper tested point is feasible
candidates.decision_reason: It avoids interpolation and adaptive-frontier logic, giving a defensible finite-grid result if refinement is unstable.

candidates.name: linear effective-volume mixing rule
candidates.formulation: Replace A and B by a single equivalent volume fraction and infer probability from the pure-A curve.
assumptions: Shape, size and cross-type connectivity affect percolation only through total weighted volume.
validation_plan: compare predicted and explicit mixed simulations
refutation_evidence: mixtures with equal effective volume have materially different spanning probabilities
rejection_evidence: A rods and B spheres have different excluded-volume and bridging behavior; the official cross-type threshold makes a one-dimensional linear equivalence unsupported.
candidates.decision_reason: It removes the mechanism the question is designed to evaluate.

fallback_model: coarse non-dominated grid with independent confirmation
stop_conditions: Q1/Q2 kernels are not approved and validated
no candidate achieves the probability constraint within the declared domain
compute cap prevents resolving the cheapest frontier neighborhood
